subject: Horizon Health — unexpected 429s and latency spike affecting production
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@horizonhealth.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: Triage@horizonhealth.io
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:43 -0700
Subject: Production impact — 429s + high latency since 08:50 PDT

Hi Grace / Redwood team,

We've been seeing a sharp increase in 429s and 500ms+ tail latency starting ~08:50 PDT this morning for our /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings routes. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 6.7% and end-user requests are timing out for some flows. Our product team is getting customer reports.

Attached are a 5‑minute sample of logs and a trace from two affected pods (horizon-prod-1/2). We saw repeated 429 responses with X-RateLimit-Reason: "burst_quota_exceeded" and tokens_per_minute spikes in bursts that align with a marketing campaign.

Can your ops team triage urgently? We are in a live window for a partner demo in an hour.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Wu
Head of Platform Engineering — Horizon Health
Attachment: horizon_request_logs_20260901.txt (text)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@horizonhealth.io>, support@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:20:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — 429s + high latency since 08:50 PDT

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm escalating to SRE and product. Short plan:
- Karthik & Sean: immediate triage to confirm whether this is quota/burst policy enforcement vs. upstream contention.
- I'll request a temporary burst allowance increase if we confirm a burst-window mismatch.
- Neha: I'll coordinate comms and a short MA (mutual action) with Horizon.

I'll keep you posted in the thread.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:45:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — 429s + high latency since 08:50 PDT

Quick summary from logs and control-plane snapshot:
- Observed sustained short burst traffic: 30s windows with request rate spikes ~6x baseline.
- Customer's account is on a reserved plan with a low burst_window (30s) and modest burst_credits. When the marketing job fires, it exhausts the burst credits and the rate limiter starts returning 429s with reason "burst_quota_exceeded".
- Concurrently, queue depth increased on the shared serving pool causing tail latency to climb (we're seeing request queuing and token generation stalls).

Attachments: burst_policy_snapshot_20260901.json (policy details).

Immediate recommendations:
1) Temporary mitigation (now): add +100% temporary burst allowance for Horizon for the next 2 hours on their account (preemptive override). This should reduce 429s quickly.
2) Medium (2–24h): move heavy batch traffic to a scheduled window or route it to dedicated capacity if they want sustained headroom.
3) Postmortem: reconcile billing/plan expectations vs. observed burst patterns; update docs to call out marketing-triggered spikes.

I'm standing by to push the override if authorized. Note: a large temporary override will raise our token utilization; ops should confirm capacity before we approve across the pool.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Servicing Runtime Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Alex Wu <alex.wu@horizonhealth.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 10:05:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — 429s + high latency since 08:50 PDT

Update: we've applied a temporary +100% burst allowance to Horizon's account (effective immediately) and increased the burst_window for their plan from 30s -> 120s for the next 2 hours. Early signs: 429 rate dropped from 6.7% to 0.9% in the last 6 minutes.

We are still seeing elevated p95/p99 latency (p99 ~720ms) due to queuing on the shared serving pool. Possible short-term options:
- Route Horizon traffic to a warm dedicated pool (requires approval, will take ~12–18 minutes to scale).
- Route heavy batch jobs to off-peak hours (coordination with Horizon).
- Apply a short-term SLA credit if this materially impacted the demo (ops + finance + commercial to decide).

Alex: can you confirm whether the marketing bursts are expected to continue in the next 2 hours? If so, we recommend the dedicated pool path; otherwise the temporary override should hold.

Sean Gallagher
Traffic & Capacity — Redwood Inference
Attachment: MA-plan-horizon-0926.pdf (mutual action plan draft)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Alex Wu <alex.wu@horizonhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 10:33:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — 429s + high latency since 08:50 PDT

Thanks team — good quick response. Two asks to close this loop:
1) Grace / Neha: please confirm with Horizon whether they want a short dedicated warm pool for the next 24h window. If yes, I'll fast-track approval for a one-time capacity bump; include expected traffic profile in the MA.
2) Karthik / Sean: capture the concrete root cause (burst_window too small for their observed burst shape) in the incident ticket and recommend an account-level config change plus product doc language.

If Horizon suffered demonstrable customer-impact during their partner demo, authorize Neha to discuss a goodwill credit with the commercial lead. We should treat this as an exec-attention incident given the demo risk and the pattern repeating across similar accounts in the last month.

I'll set a 1‑hour post‑incident sync for 11:45 PDT to review data, then prepare a short exec note (to be shared with Customer Success leadership).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
